title: Control Plane Evidence Graph
assertions: every evidence chain must connect observation, hypothesis, change, verifier, evidence, decision, and next loop
change and verifier refs must point to existing repository files or package directories
artifact evidence refs are names only and must stay redacted
evidence graph records explain why a loop exists without relying on narrative memory
frontend handoff decisions that change thread semantics must connect to the closed-loop claim that enforces them
cross-repository lifecycle observations must become owned open questions when this repository cannot safely change the runtime owner
evidence graph evidence must publish generated_at and expires_at and refresh on a schedule
evidence graph refresh evidence must expose workflow_file, cadence_minutes, and manual_refresh_command, and the workflow must upload the evidence artifact with strict if-no-files-found behavior

chains.observation: Provider and smoke harness failures could previously end as isolated artifacts.
chains.hypothesis: Redacted harness summaries can be transformed into closed-loop candidate records.
chains.decision: Harness failures are promoted into closed-loop candidate artifacts that require claim binding, verifier, CI gate, redacted evidence, decision record, and evidence graph edge before adoption.

chains.observation: Redacted live workflow summaries could be reused after or exactly at their evidence expiry boundary, allowing stale harness output to create fresh closed-loop candidates.
chains.hypothesis: Stamping generated_at and expires_at in the redacted summary, then requiring generated_at < expires_at and now < expires_at in harness promotion, prevents stale observations from entering the closed-loop backlog.
chains.decision: Harness promotion now treats evidence freshness as a strict merge gate: malformed windows, zero-length windows, expired summaries, and exact-expiry summaries cannot produce closed-loop candidate evidence.

chains.observation: The provider acceptance harness declared codex_provider_qa, openclaw_provider_qa, and daemon_runtime_snapshot observations, but the redacted smoke summary or loop manifest could omit structured provider coverage while still reporting generic contract coverage.
chains.hypothesis: Binding those observations to workflow source phrases, summary claims, machine-readable provider coverage, and the ai_thread_history loop identity lets agents see which provider/runtime paths and live v3 thread-history API surfaces were verified without reading raw live output or exporting secrets.
chains.decision: Provider acceptance evidence now exposes codex, OpenClaw, daemon runtime snapshot, and live v3 thread-history smoke coverage in the safe redacted summary path, while loop-registry evidence exposes codex/openclaw provider coverage and rejects observation/provider drift before merge; the same scheduled smoke artifact is also owned by ai_thread_history so product thread regressions are visible as loop evidence instead of only provider QA evidence.

chains.observation: Claim semantic hashes can become self-referential if semantic_hash metadata values inside bound generated files are treated as semantic input.
chains.hypothesis: Normalizing semantic_hash metadata values before hashing preserves real statement, policy, verifier, and bound-file meaning changes while preventing evidence refresh metadata from becoming its own meaning change.
chains.decision: Semantic hash metadata is now hash-inert evidence metadata; claim hashes still move when semantic content or bound executable surfaces move.

chains.observation: The AI Agent load harness produced useful stress evidence, but failures could remain a standalone load artifact instead of becoming a closed-loop adoption candidate.
chains.hypothesis: Scheduling the load harness and routing its redacted live summary through harness promotion lets performance or reliability failures enter the same candidate intake path as smoke failures.
chains.decision: Load/stress failures now have the same closed-loop promotion path as smoke failures: daily evidence refresh, redacted summary, candidate artifact, intake, and decision records.

chains.observation: Control-plane high-traffic risk surfaces had isolated benchmarks, pprof configuration, live load tooling, local pressure findings, and per-run resource rows, but agents still needed a per-scenario capacity estimate to compare concurrent-user pressure without recalculating raw rows; pressure output could also promote a zero goroutine delta as if it were an actionable leak signal, heavy local stress needed to stay separate from the lightweight CI pressure command, the static audit could lose an entire endpoint, DB, SSE, scheduling, fanout, waiter, progress, lock, read-model, or goroutine-risk category while still reporting a non-empty surface list, live HTTP load evidence lacked direct throughput, failure-rate, endpoint-finding, load-generator resource rows, and opt-in pprof sample metadata, local pressure had resource deltas but no same-command CPU/heap/goroutine profile metadata path for manual hotspot inspection, the v3 thread history endpoint needed httptest pressure coverage rather than only internal projection timing, local pressure showed client event subscriber fanout as a measurable allocation/cpu hotspot before any endpoint contract change, the generated evidence artifacts did not directly expose assertion/category coverage even though the manifest verified those rules, follow-up pressure showed progress ingest repeatedly allocating around 590KB/op while appending monotonically increasing lines, benchmark profiling showed runtime progress lookups copying client-visible thread lines before internal state checks, pressure candidates still carried human TODO wording instead of executable next-step commands, assignment long-poll/tool-approval waiter risks were claimed as hot paths without direct local pressure scenarios measuring waiter timer/goroutine behavior, and candidate artifacts did not carry the measured capacity/latency/allocation/cpu summary needed for the next loop to prioritize without reopening the raw pressure report.
chains.hypothesis: A control-plane performance sidecar can verify hot-path files, benchmark/test functions, local open-loop pressure evidence, explicit local pressure scenario names, manual high-concurrency pressure evidence commands, optional local CPU/heap/goroutine profile metadata with 0600 profile files, per-scenario capacity estimates, measured alloc/latency/cpu/subscriber findings, positive-only goroutine leak findings, pprof loopback command, redacted aiagentload command, live aiagentload throughput/capacity/resource findings, opt-in pprof sample metadata without profile bodies, required high-traffic category coverage, assertion/category coverage fields in the evidence artifact, allocation-aware progress merge/filter surfaces, runtime progress raw lookup surfaces, line-retention regression tests, bounded assignment/tool-approval waiter pressure scenarios, finding-level closed-loop adoption plans whose commands are directly executable, and candidate measurement summaries that carry max concurrent users, ops/sec, p95 latency, alloc/op, cpu/op, goroutine delta, and error-free status, then publish candidate evidence for architect review.

Live progress fanout also precomputes the client-visible progress payload once per event before subscriber visibility checks, progress line ingestion avoids copying the whole existing line slice or allocating a seen-seq map for strictly increasing line batches, runtime progress lookup avoids client-visible thread copies on internal hot paths, runtime thread lines are retained before snapshot persistence, pressure operations can now clean up scenario-owned resources, pressure candidate adoption plans now expose executable go run/go test commands for each required next artifact, and candidate artifacts now carry measured capacity/latency/allocation/cpu summaries for the next loop, preserving v2/v3 contracts while reducing repeated progress allocation work and keeping next-loop handoff machine-runnable.

chains.observation: A harness workflow can run harnesspromotion in the happy path but skip promotion or candidate artifact upload after the smoke/load step fails, and a newly registered harness loop can be omitted from the harness-promotion source manifest entirely.
chains.hypothesis: Verifying that both the harnesspromotion step and closed-loop candidate artifact upload step run under if: always(), and that every registered harness loop has exactly one promotion source with the same refresh workflow, keeps failed harness runs from becoming silent artifacts.
chains.decision: Harness promotion is now verified as a failure-path behavior and a source-coverage contract: registered harness failures must still produce closed-loop candidate evidence, and new harness loops cannot skip harness-promotion source coverage.

chains.observation: Closed-loop candidates named required artifact types, but the candidate artifact did not itself carry executable commands for producing or verifying those artifacts; later producer-source growth also showed adoption plans can become passive if intake and decision loops do not consume every producer source, intake evidence did not expose adoption commands without reopening the candidate artifact, and producer workflow changes could avoid the intake or decision verifier path.
chains.hypothesis: Embedding an adoption_plan in each candidate, exposing candidate_adoption_plans and producer-emitted candidate_subjects in intake evidence, verifying producer-source coverage in intake plus decision seed coverage, and binding each source workflow to intake/decision path triggers lets agents act from evidence artifacts even if they do not read the surrounding documentation.
chains.decision: Candidate artifacts now carry an adoption_plan, intake evidence exposes candidate_adoption_plans, candidate intake and decision evidence preserve producer-emitted candidate_subjects beside adoption and decision metadata, intake must cover every closed_loop_candidate producer source, decision verification requires an owned seed for every intake source, and producer workflow changes must trigger intake plus decision verification while still rejecting candidates whose plan does not cover every required next artifact.

chains.observation: Closed-loop candidate artifacts required an evidence_graph_edge follow-up, but the candidate record did not name the concrete harness-to-closed-loop edge it was created from.
chains.hypothesis: Embedding promotion_edge in candidates, exposing promotion_edges in harness promotion evidence plus intake and decision evidence, and binding the claim to harness-failure observation plus verifier and CI coverage lets agents follow the failure-to-closed-loop path without reading narrative docs.
chains.decision: Candidate artifacts now carry promotion_edge, harness promotion evidence carries the deduplicated promotion_edges list, intake consumes smoke/load/performance producer sources, decision verification rejects drift between the candidate edge and its source harness target, and loop closure audit regression keeps the promotion-edge claim from returning as an unbound coverage gap.

chains.observation: Closed-loop candidate artifacts exposed source freshness at the artifact envelope, but an individual candidate item could be copied without its source workflow, run, expiry context, or claim-coverage dimensions.
chains.hypothesis: Embedding source_ref in each candidate, exposing candidate_source_refs in intake and decision evidence, verifying source_ref drift, and binding the source_ref claim to observe/verify/fail coverage keeps harness evidence context attached even when agents consume candidate items without reading surrounding docs.
chains.decision: Candidate artifacts now carry per-candidate source_ref, intake and decision evidence expose candidate_source_refs for every consumed producer source, verification rejects source_ref drift or missing source run identity, and loop closure audit regression keeps the source-ref claim from returning as an unbound coverage gap.

chains.observation: Added business claims, changed claims, generated-doc bindings, or removed claims could change without bound code or tests changing in the same pull request.
chains.hypothesis: Comparing the PR diff against the loop registry can force claim additions, claim meaning changes, generated-doc binding changes, and claim removals to co-change bound code or test paths, not just manifests or generated docs.
chains.decision: PR impact verification rejects claim additions, claim meaning changes, generated-doc binding changes, and claim removals when the diff only changes manifests or generated docs; at least one bound code or test path must move, and the claim coverage tokens now make that enforcement visible to the loop-closure audit.

chains.observation: A business claim meaning change could co-change bound code or tests while leaving generated claim evidence or the evidence graph reasoning chain stale.
chains.hypothesis: Requiring generated claim evidence and the evidence graph reasoning manifest to change with claim meaning changes keeps human-readable generated surfaces, Observation, Hypothesis, Decision, and Next Loop aligned with the changed claim.
chains.decision: Claim meaning impact now requires generated claim evidence and reasoning evidence movement, preventing code/test-only claim edits from bypassing generated docs or the evidence graph, and its claim coverage tokens make that generated-evidence and reasoning-chain requirement visible to the loop-closure audit.

chains.observation: A claim-bound code or test path could change with only manifest evidence, or with generated-doc evidence while leaving the evidence graph reasoning chain stale.
chains.hypothesis: Requiring generated-doc evidence and evidence graph reasoning movement for claim-bound executable surface changes keeps human-readable generated surfaces, Observation, Hypothesis, Decision, and Next Loop aligned even when the claim statement itself does not change.
chains.decision: Bound executable surface changes now require reasoning evidence movement in addition to claim evidence, preventing code/test-only drift from bypassing the evidence graph.

chains.observation: Loop registry impact evidence exposed changed_file_count but not the actual changed repository paths, forcing agents and reviewers to rerun git diff before understanding PR impact scope.
chains.hypothesis: Publishing a sorted changed_files list in the impact evidence makes the impact verifier output self-contained and lets downstream agents infer semantic scope from evidence alone.
chains.decision: Impact evidence now includes changed_files alongside changed_file_count, so PR impact scope is executable evidence rather than an implicit git-diff side channel.

chains.observation: The loop registry could reject semantic drift internally while its evidence artifact did not show each claim's code, test, manifest, generated doc, verifier, target command, and evidence-chain surface to downstream agents.
chains.hypothesis: Publishing per-claim surface evidence with target verifier commands and evidence graph chain ids, then rejecting manifest-only claims without code or test paths, lets agents infer the required co-change, QA, and reasoning scope from machine evidence instead of relying on narrative docs or memory.
chains.decision: Claim surface binding, target verifier commands, and evidence graph chain ids are now visible in loop-registry evidence and generated docs, and manifest-only claims are rejected so AI agents can detect executable code/test, QA, and reasoning scope from verifier output even when they skip prose.

chains.observation: Loop manifests declared verifies labels, but those labels could remain prose-like tokens that were not mapped to a concrete claim, verifier surface, or machine-readable failure condition.
chains.hypothesis: Adding covers_verifies, covers_observes, and covers_fails_when to claim bindings, then rejecting uncovered or unknown tokens, lets the loop registry derive QA scope and regression semantics from the manifest instead of relying on a human to interpret loop labels.
chains.decision: Loop verifies tokens are now executable coverage requirements: every token must be claimed by a business claim in the same loop, claim surfaces expose which verifies tokens they close, and loop-closure audit keeps the verifies coverage claim from returning as a claim-coverage candidate.

chains.observation: Loop coverage verification for observes, verifies, fails_when, and evidence used separate per-dimension algorithms, and the resulting coverage axes were not exposed as first-class evidence, so a future coverage axis or behavior change required agents to remember multiple files instead of reading one executable semantic table.
chains.hypothesis: A static loop coverage dimension registry can bind each axis to loop token extraction, claim token extraction, completion checking, top-level verification dispatch, evidence JSON, and generated docs, while registry and evidence tests prove every axis has executable handlers and a machine-readable surface.
chains.decision: Loop coverage dimensions now share one executable registry; observes, verifies, fails_when, and evidence coverage still keep their public verifier wrappers, but behavior changes must co-change through the registry, evidence JSON, generated docs, and registry/evidence tests instead of scattered per-axis implementations.

chains.observation: Loop manifests declared observes labels, but those labels could remain prose-like tokens that were not mapped to a concrete claim, evidence surface, or machine-readable failure condition.
chains.hypothesis: Adding covers_observes and covers_fails_when to claim bindings and rejecting uncovered or unknown tokens lets the loop registry derive observation scope and failure semantics from the manifest instead of relying on a human to interpret loop labels.
chains.decision: Loop observes tokens are now executable coverage requirements: every token must be claimed by a business claim in the same loop, claim surfaces expose which observes tokens they close, and loop-closure audit keeps the observation coverage claim from returning as a claim-coverage candidate.

chains.observation: Loop manifests declared fails_when labels, but those labels could remain prose-like tokens that were not mapped to a concrete claim and verifier surface, or the claim could lack observe/fail tokens that classify missing failure coverage as a regression.
chains.hypothesis: Adding covers_fails_when to claim bindings, rejecting uncovered or unknown tokens, and binding the rule to regression_pattern observations lets the loop registry derive failure semantics from the manifest instead of relying on a human to interpret loop labels.
chains.decision: Loop fails_when tokens are now executable coverage requirements: every token must be claimed by a business claim in the same loop, claim surfaces expose which failure conditions they close, and loopclosureaudit keeps the rule bound to explicit regression and claim-without-verifier failure tokens.

chains.observation: Loop manifests declared evidence source paths, but those paths could remain artifact labels that were not mapped to a concrete claim and evidence surface, or the claim could lack observe/fail tokens that tell agents this is an evidence-expiry and regression-pattern rule.
chains.hypothesis: Adding covers_evidence to claim bindings, rejecting uncovered or unknown evidence paths, and binding the claim to evidence_expired/regression_pattern observations lets the loop registry derive artifact-to-claim meaning from the manifest instead of relying on a human to interpret artifact names.
chains.decision: Loop evidence source paths are now executable coverage requirements: every path must be claimed by a business claim in the same loop, claim surfaces expose which evidence artifacts they close, and loopclosureaudit keeps the rule bound to explicit evidence-expiry observe/fail tokens.

chains.observation: Loop evidence sources had machine-readable paths, but their kind field could drift into free-form values before product QA evidence such as API snapshots or screenshots became first-class evidence modalities.
chains.hypothesis: Declaring evidence kinds as a Loop Registry vocabulary and rejecting unknown kinds makes QA modalities executable: agents can add json, workflow artifact, generated doc, API snapshot, or screenshot evidence only through known system language.
chains.decision: Loop evidence kinds are now an executable vocabulary, including future product QA modalities api_snapshot and screenshot, and loopregistry verification rejects unknown free-form evidence kind values.

chains.observation: Loop registry evidence exposed graph edge counts, but not the actual loop-to-claim or harness-to-candidate edge list, and the graph-edge claim did not expose the harness failure and claim coverage failure semantics it closes.
chains.hypothesis: Publishing executable evidence_graph edges, verifying each harness promotes_to target has a matching promotes_failure_to edge, requiring every claim to have a loop-owned enforces edge, and declaring harness_failure/regression/failure coverage lets agents infer claim enforcement and harness promotion paths directly from machine evidence.
chains.decision: Loop registry evidence now carries graph edges, rejects both harness promotes_to targets without matching promotion edges and claim bindings without loop-owned enforces edges, and loop-closure audit keeps the graph-edge claim bound to harness failure and claim coverage failure semantics.

chains.observation: Claim verifier commands, PR impact changed files, changed claim ids, changed claim generated evidence, reasoning evidence, and claim-bound surface scope existed in the loop-registry evidence artifact, but a reviewer or agent still had to open artifacts or run jq before seeing the exact target QA command or changed semantic surfaces in a PR check.
chains.hypothesis: Emitting GitHub Actions annotations from the same loop-registry evidence surface makes target verifier commands, impact changed files, changed claims, changed claim generated evidence, reasoning evidence, and claim-bound surfaces visible in CI without adding another narrative handoff.
chains.decision: Loop-registry PR checks now surface claim verifier commands, impact changed files, changed claim ids, changed claim generated evidence, reasoning evidence, and bound claim surfaces as GitHub annotations, and the claim coverage tokens keep that annotation requirement visible to loop-closure audit even when artifacts and prose are skipped.

chains.observation: Evidence graph impact verification could fail or pass while reviewers and agents still had to open artifacts to see which changed files, observation-hypothesis-change-verifier-evidence chain ids, executable refs, claims, and next-loop targets were in scope.
chains.hypothesis: Emitting GitHub Actions annotations from the evidence graph impact surface makes changed files, changed evidence chain ids, executable refs, claim ids, and next-loop targets visible in the PR check output, so agents can repair the executable reasoning graph without reading narrative docs first.
chains.decision: Evidence graph PR checks now emit redacted GitHub annotations for changed file samples, changed chain impact, executable refs, claim ids, and next-loop targets, keeping reasoning drift actionable in the check output itself.

chains.observation: Harness-like workflow names could be added without being registered as harness loops, explicitly excluded from harness ownership, or bound to observe/verify/fail tokens that tell agents this is a harness-failure promotion rule.
chains.hypothesis: Scanning smoke, load, and harness workflow filenames, requiring either a harness loop registration or a reasoned exclusion, and binding the claim to harness_failure/regression_pattern observations keeps new QA workflows bound to closed-loop promotion semantics.
chains.decision: Smoke, load, and harness workflow additions now fail loop-registry verification unless they are registered as failure-promoting harness loops or explicitly excluded with a machine-readable reason, and loopclosureaudit keeps that rule bound to explicit harness failure observe/verify/fail tokens.

chains.observation: Deleting an AI Agent can accidentally remove or hide historical task thread replies if the read model depends on the live agent row.
chains.hypothesis: Capturing an agent snapshot on the thread and falling back to that snapshot for deleted agents keeps prior replies, results, and progress visible.
chains.decision: Deleted-agent thread retention is a closed-loop claim: historical AI thread records use captured agent snapshots instead of disappearing with the mutable agent row.

chains.observation: A user reply inside an AI Agent thread can disappear after refresh if v3 history only projects the latest agent status, and conversational execution-approval replies such as go command requests can accidentally create new work when there is no pending tool approval to decide.
chains.hypothesis: Persisting user follow-up messages as thread history rows, replaying them into v3 history, routing affirmative execution replies only to same-assignment pending tool approvals, and fail-closing stale approval replies preserves human-agent 티키타카 after reload without turning approval chat into replacement assignment history.
chains.decision: User follow-up retention is enforced as v3 history behavior, not frontend memory. Explicit command-execution replies close existing pending tool approvals, generic follow-up phrases remain normal work messages, and approval-shaped replies without a pending approval are recorded as terminal guidance instead of creating replacement assignment history.

chains.observation: Two different AI Agents can use the same provider runtime, so provider-based dedupe can collapse independent task assignments and threads.
chains.hypothesis: Assignment and thread identity must stay agent/assignment scoped even when provider/runtime_kind is identical.
chains.decision: Same-provider multi-assignment is a thread identity claim: provider/runtime labels are display metadata, not dedupe keys.

chains.observation: Frontend implementation needed a stable key to distinguish same-agent reassignment from follow-up replies inside an existing AI Agent comment card, later observed stale queued_by_busy_agent status text appearing next to newer progress or running state in the same conversation, and staging showed a task screen keeping an optimistic running spinner even though daemon status had running_tasks=0, v2 thread-stream-subscription returned active_thread_filters=[], and v3 history contained only terminal threads. A running thread state can be known before a delayed queued status message receives a later observed_at timestamp, and terminal server truth must be able to clear stale client session state.
chains.hypothesis: Binding conversation_id, parent_thread_id, queued-status current-only filtering, and terminal active_stream closure to the v3 thread history contract, generated frontend handoff, runtime projection tests, and loop-registry claim prevents provider or agent based dedupe from collapsing distinct conversations, prevents stale queue hints from rendering as durable agent replies once progress, active running state, or result history exists, and lets refresh/refetch clear local running UI when every server-side thread is terminal.
chains.decision: AI Thread History v3 comment card grouping is a closed-loop claim: conversation_id groups the card, parent_thread_id links follow-up runs, same-agent reassignment receives a distinct conversation, queued_by_busy_agent is only a current status hint that v3 suppresses once the same conversation has active running state, newer progress, or result history regardless of delayed queued-message timestamps, and terminal-only v3 history omits active_stream so a client refetch can clear stale optimistic running UI.

chains.observation: Thread history consumers can misread a completed run followed by a queued follow-up if the response reuses execution identity or leaves same-timestamp messages in an unstable order.
chains.hypothesis: Binding follow-up replies to a new assignment-scoped run identity, then sorting user, progress seq, and agent result messages deterministically, keeps v3 history replayable after refresh without frontend heuristics.
chains.decision: AI Thread History v3 execution identity and message ordering are closed-loop invariants: follow-up work gets a fresh assignment/run axis, and same-timestamp messages sort by user intent, progress sequence, then agent result.

chains.observation: On staging, stopping an AI Agent task and immediately assigning again could make the just-stopped agent appear to keep working, and a stop call without an active assignment could create a synthetic stopped thread with no assignment_id.
chains.hypothesis: Separating stop target selection from unassign target selection keeps user stop strongly scoped to active assignment threads, while preserving participant-removal history semantics for unassign.
chains.decision: Stop/reassign consistency is now a closed-loop invariant: stop cannot invent synthetic thread history or rewrite completed history when no active assignment exists, and unassign keeps the separate participant-removal behavior.

chains.observation: Loop registry and evidence graph evidence could prove shape but not freshness because the artifacts lacked generated_at and expires_at, the evidence graph workflow did not run unless code changed, or the claim lacked observe/verify/fail tokens that classify it as an evidence-expiry closed-loop rule.
chains.hypothesis: Self-expiring evidence artifacts plus a scheduled evidence graph workflow whose cadence fits the TTL, publishes strict evidence, and keeps the claim bound to evidence_expired observations let tools detect stale reasoning evidence and refresh it without a human reminder.
chains.decision: Core loop reasoning evidence now carries a 24h freshness window, exposes its manual refresh command and cadence, verifies that the scheduled evidence graph workflow uploads the evidence artifact strictly before it can be treated as fresh, and loopclosureaudit keeps the rule bound to explicit evidence-expiry observe/verify/fail tokens.

chains.observation: Closed-loop candidate artifacts could be produced without a scheduled intake verifier that reads them, new producer sources such as control-plane performance could remain passive if intake only consumed older smoke/load artifacts, PR checks could miss whether performance-shaped candidates are actually consumed, and live scheduled runs could fail before publishing evidence when a producer had no candidate artifact for that cycle.
chains.hypothesis: A candidate intake tool can require explicit redacted candidate input for verifier runs, verify producer, loop registry, graph, adoption artifact requirements, fail when any closed_loop_candidate producer source is missing from intake, consume a performance-specific candidate fixture in PR checks, and let scheduled live aggregation emit skipped evidence for missing producer artifacts instead of dropping the evidence file.

chains.observation: The loop registry verifier was upgraded to check every expiring loop, but the registry wording could still describe only 24h loops, or the claim could lack observe/verify/fail tokens that tell agents this is an evidence-expiry closed-loop rule.
chains.hypothesis: Promoting the refresh-scope rule to a claim, rejecting stale 24h-only wording, and binding the claim to evidence_expired/regression_pattern observations with verifier and failure tokens keeps the SSOT, verifier, and generated reader aligned.
chains.decision: All expiring loops, including long-expiry queues, are now covered by scheduled refresh verification, stale 24h-only SSOT language fails, and loopclosureaudit keeps the claim bound to explicit evidence-expiry observe/verify/fail tokens.

chains.observation: A refresh workflow can be edited without carrying the loop id it refreshes, or the claim that guards that workflow can omit observe/verify/fail coverage tokens, leaving agents to infer semantic ownership from file names or prose.
chains.hypothesis: Requiring RIIDO_LOOP_IDS in every refresh workflow and claim coverage tokens for that requirement makes loop ownership executable and lets the registry and loop-closure verifiers catch workflow-only or claim-only drift.
chains.decision: Refresh workflows now declare their loop identities directly, and the guarding claim exposes coverage tokens plus regression coverage, so workflow-only or claim-only edits cannot silently detach scheduled QA from the loop registry.

chains.observation: Loop registry evidence exposed refresh workflow maps, cadence maps, claim surfaces, and refresh plans separately, but an agent still had to compose and order the manual QA refresh command, claim verifier command set, evidence artifact set, and next refresh/expiry timestamps itself, and the refresh-plan claim did not expose the evidence-expiry failure semantics it closes.
chains.hypothesis: A per-loop refresh_plans evidence surface with generated_at, next_refresh_due_at, evidence_expires_at, claim ids, verifier commands, ordered next commands, artifacts, refresh commands, and explicit evidence_expired coverage lets agents and reviewers identify expired-evidence QA actions directly from machine evidence.
chains.decision: Loop registry evidence now exposes refresh_plans with workflow, cadence, expiry, next refresh due time, evidence expiry time, claim ids, verifier commands, ordered next commands, evidence artifacts, and manual refresh commands for every loop, and loop-closure audit keeps the refresh-plan claim bound to evidence-expiry failure semantics.

chains.observation: Loop registry evidence could expose ordered next_commands while still leaving scheduled automation to decide which commands to select and publish after the evidence artifact expires, the selected command queue itself could be timeless, and the claim surface did not expose observe/verify/fail coverage tokens for that expired-evidence command selection gate.
chains.hypothesis: A refresh command selection mode in the scheduled workflow that reads existing loop-registry evidence, emits only expired refresh plan commands, uploads a strict command artifact with its own generated_at/expires_at window, and binds the claim coverage tokens turns stale evidence into a machine-executable QA queue without creating immortal commands.
chains.decision: Expired loop-registry evidence can be consumed as input and transformed into an uploaded ordered refresh command artifact with its own 24-hour freshness window; a manifest-level regression now proves every declared loop, including longer-cadence weekly loops, becomes selected when its evidence window expires, and loopclosureaudit keeps that expired-evidence command selection rule claim-bound through explicit observe/verify/fail coverage tokens.

chains.observation: CI could catch claim binding drift, but local commits still depended on humans remembering the verifier and the claim did not expose the regression/failure semantics it closes.

chains.observation: CI could catch evidence graph chain drift, but local commits still depended on humans remembering the evidencegraph impact verifier before opening a PR.

chains.observation: A staging runtime settings page can show a local daemon offline after the desktop app gracefully stops its desktop-managed daemon on app quit, and open decisions can still strand humans if the queue names only a next artifact without a bounded next command.

chains.decision: Desktop daemon lifecycle/profile ownership remains an executable open decision until a desktop-owned manifest defines app quit, profile isolation, and stop-source evidence behavior; every open decision now also exposes a bounded next command in evidence so the follow-up action is not trapped in operator memory.

loop.observation: Evidence artifacts existed, but the reasoning chain from observation to next loop was still scattered across generated readers and PR memory.
loop.hypothesis: A compact evidence graph can make the development loop navigable by tools without asking an AI to read every narrative document.
loop.execute: Verify every chain has observation, hypothesis, change, verifier, evidence, decision, and next-loop nodes; verify repository refs exist; generate this reader and publish graph evidence in CI.
loop.evaluate: The verifier fails on incomplete chains, duplicate ids, missing refs, stale generated docs, missing strict workflow evidence, or missing redaction on artifact evidence.
loop.retrospective: This makes the evidence loop itself inspectable: future agents can see why a loop exists, what changed, what verifies it, and what loop should run next.
